title: Credit Card Minimum Payments: The 17-Year Trap (The Math)

lines.say: Minimum payment due: a hundred and fifty dollars.
It looks manageable. That's the point.

scene.label: Credit card · 24% APR
scene.sub: a common minimum: 1% of the balance + that month's interest

lines.cap: Here's a $5,000 balance at 24%. Many cards set the minimum at 1% of the balance, plus that month's interest.
lines.say: Here's a five thousand dollar balance at twenty-four percent. Many cards set the minimum at one percent of the balance, plus that month's interest.

lines.cap: So the first minimum is $150. $100 of it is interest. Only $50 touches the balance.
lines.say: So the first minimum is a hundred and fifty. A hundred of it is interest. Only fifty touches the balance.
Here's why that number keeps you paying for years.
The trap. The minimum shrinks as you pay.

lines.cap: A year in, it's down to $134. By year five, $83. By year ten, $45.
lines.say: A year in, it's down to one thirty-four. By year five, eighty-three. By year ten, forty-five.
It feels like progress. But a smaller payment means the balance barely moves.

lines.cap: Paying only the minimum takes 201 months. Almost 17 years. And $8,442 in interest. More than the original balance.
lines.say: Paying only the minimum takes two hundred and one months. Almost seventeen years. And eighty-four forty-two in interest. More than the original balance.
The fix is simple. Freeze the payment.
Paying the shrinking minimum: two hundred and one months.

lines.cap: Keep paying the first minimum, $150, every month, even as the minimum drops: 56 months, and $3,322 in interest.
lines.say: Keep paying the first minimum, a hundred and fifty, every month, even as the minimum drops. Fifty-six months, and thirty-three twenty-two in interest.

lines.cap: Pay $250, and it's gone in 26 months, for $1,449.
lines.say: Pay two fifty, and it's gone in twenty-six months, for fourteen forty-nine.

scene.text: Your statement already shows this math.

lines.say: And here's something most people skip. In the US, your card statement has a box showing how long minimum payments will take, and the monthly payment that clears it in three years.

scene.label: To pay it off in 3 years
scene.sub: a month: look for this number on your statement

lines.cap: For this card, that's about $197 a month. Gone in three years.
lines.say: For this card, that's about one ninety-seven a month. Gone in three years.

scene.head: THIS WEEK
items: Find the minimum-payment box on your statement
Freeze your payment at today's minimum or more
Set autopay to that fixed amount
Send raises and windfalls at it

lines.say: So, this week.
Find the minimum-payment box on your statement.
Freeze your payment at today's minimum, or more.
Set autopay to that fixed amount, not the minimum.
And send raises and windfalls straight at it.
